original_benchmark: AppBench (AfterQuery; held-out evaluation prompts not public)
benchmark_run: AppBench public tasks (HF 'AppBench vExternal.csv', 6 tasks / 151 rubric items), one-shot source generation + LLM-judge static review -- public tasks, not held-out
substitute_gap: Public tasks, not held-out; the app is generated as source in one response and graded by static code review, not built, deployed, or functionally tested by two human graders as in AppBench.
item_ids: all 6 public tasks (#1 Financial Dashboard 24, #2 Hospital Dashboard 33, #3 Legal Assistant 22, #4 Pharmacy System 25, #5 Drawing Game 23, #6 Rental Booking 24 rubric items); no sampling needed
grader: llm-judge(Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B base on Tinker, same model as actor; non-thinking, T=0, max_tokens 6144; judge v2 evidence-first)
compute_route: Tinker sampling direct (E12/code/run_e12.py, E12/code/judge_v2.py); no containers
commands: set -a; source .env; set +a; cd E12/code; /Users/arvind/.local/share/uv/tools/tinker/bin/python run_e12.py   # generation + judge v1
cd E12/code; /Users/arvind/.local/share/uv/tools/tinker/bin/python judge_v2.py   # judge v2 (primary), rescoring is offline from raw/judge_v2_<n>.json
caveats: Public tasks, not held-out. Label mandatory. New base-model arm; never pool with the original lane.
Self-judging: the judge is the same base model as the actor, so the rate is likely inflated and is not comparable to AppBench's binary human functional grading.

Judge instability: judge v1 (JSON, bare PASS/FAIL, ignored the requested reasons) scored 81/151 = 0.536 with tasks #4 and #6 all-FAIL; judge v2 (evidence-first, one line per item) scored 122/151 = 0.808 with task #4 25/25. v2 is reported because v1 did not follow its output spec; the spread (0.54 vs 0.81) is the honest uncertainty, larger than the Wilson CI.

Two parser fixes were applied after inspecting raw judge text (v1: accept string PASS/FAIL; v2: accept verdict in either pipe field, conflicting verdicts = FAIL). No model call was repeated for the parser fixes; all scores recompute from raw/*.json.
Generation for task #6 hit the 16384-token cap (truncated output), yet v2 passed 15/24 items for it -- evidence of judge leniency.
Wilson CI treats 151 items as independent; they are clustered in 6 apps, so true uncertainty is wider.
